9|Digitizing Embroidery Designs
9|
9|
9|
9|BERNINA artista provides embroiderers with
9|a fast, flexible way of creating and editing
9|embroidery designs. This section provides an
9|overview of the embroidery digitizing process
9|as it applies to BERNINA artista.
9|The BERNINA artista embroidery digitizing
9|process will consist of some or all of the
9|following stages:
9| planning designs
9| digitizing designs
9| modifying designs
9| improving design quality
9| adding lettering
9| stitching out designs
9|
9|
9|

9|                                                      stitches are angled to match shapes

10|The stitched-out design should also have the                   Design sequence
10|following characteristics:
10|                                                               The design sequence is the order in which
10| The design stitches out efficiently on the                   objects are created and therefore the order in
10|   machine.                                                    which they are stitched out. You can change the
10| The fabric has not puckered around the                       sequence of objects in the design to improve
10|   stitched areas.                                             sewing — for example, to minimize color
10| The design is free of loose ends.                            changes. Details should be stitched last. See
10|                                                               Resequencing embroidery objects for details.

10|Preparing to digitize                                                         2
10|
10|Before you start digitizing, you need to analyze
10|and plan design shapes and stitching sequence
10|carefully.
10|Design shapes need to be clearly defined to                                       details
10|make them easy to embroider. The easiest                            1                last
10|shapes to embroider have a relatively constant
10|width, with smooth edges, no sharp turns and
10|no small, protruding details.
10|                                                               Stitch types
10|                                 Simplify edges in artwork
10|                                 before or during digitizing   Decide which stitch types you will use for each
10|                                                               design shape. While you normally set stitch type
10|                                                               before digitizing each shape, BERNINA artista
10|                                                               lets you change them at any stage. See Outline
10|                                                               and Fill Stitches for details.

21|Basic Procedures
21|

21|
21|To start using BERNINA artista, you
21|need to know the basic procedures,
21|such as starting up, opening and
21|creating designs, and saving. Other
21|basic procedures include showing and
21|hiding the grid, displaying and using
21|toolbars and switching to Artistic View.
21|Security access codes control your
21|access to special options in the
21|software. You need to be able to
21|identify your system’s identity codes,
21|and enter new access codes for
21|upgrades.
21|This section describes how to start
21|BERNINA artista, how to open designs, start new ones and use the basic commands. It
21|also explains how to turn on and off the grid and measure distances on-screen. The
21|section also explains the procedure for entering security codes.

33|Viewing Designs
33|
33|
33|
33|BERNINA artista provides many viewing features to make it easier to work with your
33|design. Zoom in on an area to see more detail or view the design at actual size. Preview
33|an existing design in different colors on different fabrics.
33|
33|
33|
33|
33|BERNINA artista also provides information about designs in a variety of ways and
33|formats. Before even opening BERNINA artista or your design, you can check some
33|design information for ART files directly from Windows Explorer. You can view stitching
33|details about a design in the Design Properties dialog. Also the Print Preview provides
33|essential design information, including a design preview, the size of the design, color
33|sequence and any special instructions.
33|Show or hide various design elements with the available display settings. You can show
33|or hide needle penetration points and the stitches themselves.
33|This section explains the design viewing modes available in BERNINA artista as well as
33|the various design viewing settings. It also explains how to obtain and customize
33|information about your designs.

43|                                                                              Chapter 5

43|Selecting Objects
43|
43|
43|
43|When working with embroidery designs, you need to
43|understand the stitching sequence. You can check a design’s
43|stitching sequence in BERNINA artista by ‘traveling’ through
43|it stitch-by-stitch. You can also check the sequence by slowly
43|redrawing your design on screen.
43|BERNINA artista provides various ways to select the objects
43|that comprise an embroidery design. You can select all
43|objects to modify the design as a whole, or individual objects
43|for more precise modification.
43|This section describes how to check designs by traveling
43|through them. It describes how to select objects using the
43|selection tools and keyboard. It also shows how to select while traveling through the
43|design, or by using the Color Film. You also see how to select objects of a specific color.
43|
43|
43|
43|Selecting all objects in a design
43|Select all objects to apply changes to a whole
43|design. See also BERNINA artista Shortcut Keys.
43|
43|
43|To select all objects in a design
43|
43| Select Edit > Select All or press Ctrl + A.
43|   Sizing handles appear around the entire
43|                                                      no objects selected     all objects selected
43|   design.
43|
43|                                                   To deselect, select Edit > Deselect All, press
43|                                                     X or Esc.

59|                                                                                Chapter 7
59|
59|Digitizing Methods
59|
59|
59|
59|In BERNINA artista, you build designs from basic shapes or
59|‘embroidery objects’. Like drawing objects, embroidery
59|objects have certain defining characteristics or ‘properties’
59|such as color, size, position, and so on. They also have
59|properties unique to embroidery such as stitch type and
59|density.
59|The most important property for an embroidery object is its
59|stitch type. Different stitch types are suited to different
59|shapes. See Outline and Fill Stitches for details.
59|The process of creating embroidery objects on-screen is
59|called ‘digitizing’. Like creating designs in graphics
59|applications, this involves the use of different digitizing
59|tools. Digitizing tools in BERNINA artista are similar to
59|drawing tools except that the end result is an embroidery
59|object rather than a drawing object.
59|Object properties are defined as you digitize, but they can
59|be changed at any stage. When you create an embroidery object, you can accept the
59|default settings for the particular digitizing method, or apply new ones. Default settings
59|are stored in the design template. You can also define ‘current’ properties to influence
59|all the objects you create in the current design. See Object Properties and Templates for
59|details.
59|This section describes how to digitize shapes with the main digitizing methods. It also
59|explains how to adjust digitizing settings to obtain the best results.
59|
59|
59|
59|Digitizing tools                                     Digitizing methods divide broadly into two
59|                                                     categories — outline and fill.
59|Different digitizing methods or ‘tools’ are suited
59|to creating different shapes or design elements.
59|
59|
59|
59|
59|BERNINA® artista Online Manual                                                                    57
59|

65|                                                                                 Chapter 8
65|
65|Outline and Fill Stitches
65|
65|
65|
65|All embroidery objects in BERNINA artista have defining settings
65|or ‘properties’. Certain properties, such as size and position, are
65|common to all. Others are specific to the object type. The most
65|important property is the stitch type. Whenever you create or
65|modify an object, stitches are generated according to the
65|associated stitch type. Settings such as spacing and length can
65|also be adjusted to suit.
65|BERNINA artista provides a variety of digitizing methods or ‘tools’
65|for creating embroidery objects. The tools divide broadly into two
65|types — ‘outline’ and ‘fill’. The same applies to stitch types.
65|Outline and fill stitch types are defined whenever you create
65|embroidery shapes, but they can be changed at any stage.
65|This section explains how to select an basic outline and fill stitch
65|types, as well as change stitch settings to obtain the best results.
65|
65|
65|
65|
65|Selecting or changing stitches
65|BERNINA artista provides a number of basic          Tip Preset stitch values by changing the current
65|outline and fill stitch types. It also provides     properties in the Object Properties dialog before
65|artistic and craft stitches for special uses. See   you digitize. See Object Properties and
65|also Artistic Stitch Effects, Pattern Runs and      Templates for details.
65|Fills, and Craft Stitch Borders and Fills.
65|Different stitch types suit different shapes.
65|Whenever you create an object, it always takes
65|the currently selected stitch type. You can
65|change this at any stage.
65|

77|                                                                             Chapter 9
77|
77|Object Properties and Templates
77|
77|
77|
77|The properties of embroidery objects define general characteristics
77|such as size and position, as well as embroidery-specific
77|characteristics such as stitch type and density. The particular stitch
77|settings determine how stitches will be regenerated when you
77|reshape, transform or scale an object.
77|When you create an embroidery object, you can accept default
77|settings for the particular digitizing method, or apply new ones.
77|Default settings are stored in the design template. You can also
77|define ‘current’ properties to influence all the objects you create in
77|the current design.
77|This section explains how to change the object properties in your
77|design, as well as how to apply, create and maintain styles and
77|templates in BERNINA artista.
77|
77|
77|
77|Applying and managing object                     Default object properties
77|properties                                       Default object properties are the properties
77|                                                 stored in a design template and become the
77|BERNINA artista stores three sets of object      starting settings used when creating a new
77|properties: default, current and existing.       design based on that template.
77|
77|                                                 Current object properties
77|Note Some object properties can be modified
77|on-screen; for example, you can change the       Current object properties are the settings used
77|size properties by scaling the object with the   to create new objects. Unless you change these
77|selection handles. Other properties, such as     settings, they remain the same as the template
77|stitch spacing or length, are modified in the    defaults. You generally change them to save
77|Object Properties dialog.                        time when digitizing. For example, you may
77|                                                 preset the Step stitch spacing setting to use a
77|                                                 specific density for all new Step objects you
77|                                                 create.
77|
77|
77|
77|BERNINA® artista Online Manual                                                                  75
77|

78|
78|

78|                                                           Properties dialog. These provide access to all
78|Note The change affects new objects in the
78|                                                           the possible object properties settings.
78|design, not the template itself. To apply changes
78|to all new designs based on the current                 2 Click a tab to view the current settings and
78|template, you need to change the default — not             change as required.
78|the current — properties.

83|Thread Colors and Thread Charts
83|
83|
83|
83|When you digitize, you select thread colors for each object
83|you create from the color palette in the design window. The
83|color palette contains a selection of thread colors tailored for
83|each design. This color scheme represents the actual thread
83|colors in which a design will be stitched.
83|You can preview a design in different colors and on different
83|fabrics. In effect, you can preview multiple color schemes.
83|You can also print multiple color schemes, design
83|backgrounds, and icons of color blocks with the print preview.
83|For each color scheme, you can select colors from commercial
83|thread charts containing a range of colors from different
83|thread manufacturers, or define your own. To save time when setting up new color
83|schemes, you can create your own thread charts, using the most frequently used colors.
83|You can add, edit and delete threads from a thread chart, or rename or delete the chart
83|itself. In BERNINA artista you can search for particular threads by various criteria.
83|This section describes how to select colors from the color palette. There is also an
83|explanation of how to define your own thread colors and charts.
83|
83|

95|                                                                        Chapter 11
95|
95|Digitizing with Backdrops
95|
95|
95|
95|Artwork in both bitmap and vector format can be loaded,
95|pasted or scanned into BERNINA artista for use as
95|digitizing templates or ‘backdrops’. Textured backgrounds
95|can also be imported to show what a design will look like
95|on real fabric. Almost any artwork can be used —
95|photographs, magazine pictures, clipart drawings, and
95|even fabric samples.
95|From within BERNINA artista you can open images in MS
95|Paint, Corel PHOTO-PAINT®, or Paint Shop Pro™. Images
95|updated in this way are automatically re-imported into
95|BERNINA artista.
95|This section describes how to choose suitable artwork for
95|digitizing purposes as well as how to scan it into BERNINA artista. It also describes how
95|to digitize with images as backdrops, as well as how to show and hide them as you
95|digitize.

115|
115|Automatic Digitizing
115|
115|
115|
115|The Magic Wand tool is useful for quickly creating embroidery
115|objects from scanned images that do not require particular
115|artistic effects or embroidery-specific knowledge. This in turn
115|frees you to spend more time on the artistic or inherently
115|complicated areas of your designs.
115|BERNINA artista Auto Digitizer automatically converts artwork
115|to fully digitized embroidery with little or no intervention.
115|Various forms of artwork can be used— both bitmap and
115|vector — and various levels of user ‘assists’ applied to the
115|process.
115|With Auto Digitizer, novice embroiderers can create simple
115|designs quickly and easily. Similarly, experienced
115|embroiderers can improve productivity when working with simple designs.
115|Use PhotoSnap to create embroidery from photographs and other images.
115|This section describes how to automatically convert bitmap images to embroidery
115|designs, and create embroidery from photographs. It also describes how to digitize
115|shapes automatically with the Magic Wand and Auto Digitizer.
115|

115|automatically.

125|                                                                               Chapter 14
125|
125|Combining and Resequencing Objects
125|
125|
125|
125|BERNINA artista lets you add to designs quickly by duplicating
125|and copying existing objects. It also lets you combine designs by
125|inserting the contents of one file into another.
125|When working with embroidery designs, you need to understand
125|the stitching sequence. You can check a design’s stitching
125|sequence in BERNINA artista by ‘traveling’ through it
125|stitch-by-stitch. You can also check the sequence by slowly
125|redrawing your design on screen. Stitching sequence usually
125|occurs in the order in which the design was digitized. However,
125|you can change this by a variety of methods.
125|This section describes how to combine objects and designs by copying and pasting,
125|duplicating, and inserting techniques. It also describes how to travel through a design
125|as well as resequence objects by cut and paste, by color and with the Color Film.
125|
125|

125|another design, until replaced on the clipboard.          objects in the design.

135|                                                                             Chapter 15
135|
135|Arranging and Transforming Objects
135|
135|
135|
135|BERNINA artista allows you to change the position, size and
135|orientation of objects in a design by moving, scaling and
135|transforming them. Group objects together to apply a change
135|to them all at once. You can modify objects directly on-screen,
135|or in the Object Properties dialog.
135|This section describes how to position objects, how to group
135|and align objects, as well as how to scale, rotate, skew, and
135|mirror objects. It also shows you how to create multiple copies
135|in a wreath shape using Mirror-Merge.
135|The scalability and stitching quality of a design ultimately depends on its original source
135|– ART Grade A, ART Grade B, ART Grade C, or ART Grade D. Only native ART Grade A
135|designs contain the complete set of design information required for 100% perfect scaling
135|and transformation. See Embroidery design formats for details.
135|
135|
135|
135|Positioning objects
135|                                                    To position objects using click and drag

135|to drag them to a new position, nudging them
135|with the arrow keys or by specifying the X:Y

135|coordinates in the Object Properties dialog.        2 Click and drag the object to a new position.
135|

145|Reshaping and Editing Objects
145|
145|
145|
145|BERNINA artista lets you modify object shapes, stitch
145|angles and entry and exit points by means of control
145|points. Stitch angle lines and entry and exit markers all
145|appear around selected objects. Control points vary
145|slightly with the object type.
145|Before modifying any design, a good practice is to save
145|a copy under a new name and keep the original in case
145|you want to discard your changes and start again.
145|This section describes how to reshape objects with
145|control points, reshape circles, adjust stitch angles—including multiple stitch
145|angles—and change entry and exit points.

153|                                                                                   Chapter 17
153|
153|Editing Stitches
153|
153|
153|
153|With BERNINA artista designs, stitches are
153|automatically generated from design outlines
153|and properties. This means you can scale,
153|transform and reshape BERNINA artista
153|designs without affecting stitch density or
153|quality.
153|However, BERNINA artista also lets you edit
153|individual stitches. You simply select them like
153|any other object and move the needlepoint
153|position as required. For example, you can
153|insert stitches in an object to fill gaps. You can
153|move or delete individual or clusters of
153|selected stitches.
153|You may need to do this particularly when working with ‘stitch’ files which do not contain
153|design outline data. Where possible, however, edit the object properties rather than
153|individual stitches. See also Embroidery design formats.
153|This section deals with selecting and editing stitches.
153|
153|
153|
153|Selecting stitches                                   Selecting stitches by needle point
153|The Stitch Edit feature lets you select single        Use Stitch Edit (Edit menu) to select individual
153|stitches, several stitches, or a range of stitches    stitches for editing.
153|by selecting their needle points, or dragging a
153|bounding box around them. Selected stitches
153|                                                     You can select individual stitches in Stitch Edit
153|are highlighted in a different color.
153|                                                     mode by selecting their needle points.
153|
153|
153|                                                     Tip Zoom in and display the needle points for
153|                                                     easier selection.
153|
153|
153|
153|BERNINA® artista Online Manual                                                                           151
153|
154|                                                                                     Chapter 17: Editing Stitches
154|
154|
154|
154|To select stitches by needle point                          To select stitches with a bounding box
154|
154|1 Select Edit > Stitch Edit.                                1 Select Edit > Stitch Edit.
154|                                                            2 Drag a bounding box around the stitches you
154|                                                               want to select.
154|   Tip Press E on your keyboard to turn on
154|   Stitch Edit.                                                Stitches are selected when you release the

159|Lettering Essentials
159|
159|
159|
159|Add lettering to designs quickly and easily, either
159|on-screen using the current settings, or via the Object
159|Properties - Lettering dialog. Lettering can be edited
159|directly on-screen or with the dialog. You can apply
159|formatting to lettering objects in the same way as a word
159|processor, including italics, bolding, and right/left
159|justification. Both interactive and numeric techniques are
159|available for scaling and spacing lettering. See Alphabet
159|Samples for details.
159|This section describes how to add and edit lettering,
159|change formatting settings, and adjust lettering size and spacing.
159|
159|

159|                                                         settings in the Object Properties - Lettering
159|designs                                                  dialog. You can change them at any time. See
159|                                                         Adjusting Lettering Layout for details.

159|directly in the design window, or entering it in
159|the Object Properties - Lettering dialog.

159|                                                         4   Type the letters you want to embroider.

171|Adjusting Lettering Layout
171|
171|
171|
171|BERNINA artista gives you both interactive and precise
171|numeric control over many attributes affecting lettering
171|objects. You can adjust lettering objects as a group as
171|well as the individual letters comprising a lettering
171|object.
171|You can apply horizontal, vertical, and curved baselines
171|to your lettering objects. You can modify baseline type,
171|length, radius and angle, as well as baseline position.
171|You can numerically define the rotation angle of letters
171|relative to the baseline or the design.
171|This section describes how to adjust lettering objects as
171|well as individual letters. It also describes how to apply
171|and adjust lettering baselines.

187|create monograms quickly and easily. In BERNINA artista, all
187|of the TrueType fonts installed on your computer are available
187|to you when placing lettering on your designs.
187|This section shows you how to add symbols, create
187|monograms and use TrueType fonts in your lettering designs.

197|                                                                                  Chapter 22
197|
197|Improving Stitch Quality
197|
197|
197|
197|Use automatic underlay and pull compensation to achieve smooth,
197|even placement of stitches, and eliminate gaps in your design. These
197|features are object properties, and can be applied, removed or
197|modified at any time.
197|This section describes how to strengthen and stabilize designs with
197|automatic underlays, as well as how to compensate for fabric stretch.
197|Techniques for controlling long stitches with Auto Jump are described
197|and you will also find details of setting automatic start and end points.
197|
197|
197|
197|
197|Strengthening and stabilizing with Applying automatic underlays
197|underlays                                Use Underlay (General toolbar) to strengthen
197|                                                              and stabilize embroidery designs with
197|Underlay stitching helps stabilize fabric and                 automatic underlay.
197|reduces distortion due to the pull effect. It also
197|provides ‘loft’, raising cover stitches and            You can generate automatic underlay stitching
197|preventing them from sinking into soft fabrics.        from scratch or apply it to existing objects. The
197|When no underlay is applied, the embroidery            type of underlay you choose is determined by
197|lays flat on the fabric. It not only looks flat, but   the purpose it is to serve.
197|the underlying fabric often shows through. New
197|digitizers might be tempted to increase stitch
197|density but it is more effective to apply a proper     To apply automatic underlays
197|underlay.
197|Underlay generates underlay stitching for               Click the Auto Underlay icon with or without
197|objects based on the settings specified in the
197|                                                          objects selected.
197|Effects dialog. Underlay settings are stored with
197|each object in the same way as other object
197|properties. Thus they are regenerated
197|whenever the object is scaled or transformed.

225|Pattern Runs and Fills
225|
225|
225|
225|Patterns are pre-defined design elements,
225|such as hearts, leaves or border patterns,
225|that can be quickly inserted into a design.
225|They generally consist of one or more simple
225|objects, and are stored in a special pattern
225|set.
225|You can create your own patterns or use the
225|ones provided with the software. Patterns
225|can be scaled, rotated and mirrored in the
225|same way as other objects. You can use
225|patterns along a digitized line. You can also
225|fill shapes with rows of repeated patterns,
225|and apply special effects, using Pattern Fill.
225|This section describes how to insert patterns into your design, and how to adjust their
225|settings to get the results you want. It also explains how to create your own patterns
225|and pattern sets.
225|
225|
225|

235|                                                                                  Chapter 26
235|
235|Craft Stitch Borders and Fills
235|
235|
235|
235|BERNINA artista provides a range of craft stitches
235|which you can use in your designs to mimic some
235|traditional hand-worked embroidery. These include a
235|large range of blackwork and candlewicking patterns
235|suitable for both outlines and fill. See Craft Stitch
235|Pattern Samples for details.
235|Backstitch and stemstich are two versatile outline
235|stitches. Backstitch forms a continuous thin line,
235|similar to machine stitching, while stemstich produces
235|rope-like lines which can vary in thickness depending
235|on the angle of the stitches. Both can be used to make
235|a smooth continuous row of stitching suitable for
235|outlines and for blackwork.
235|Lacework and stipple are two decorative fill stitches.
235|Lacework can be used to give a lacey look to objects
235|such as flowers. Stippling, also known as vermicelli, is a free flowing running stitch that
235|can be used for decorative effects or to produce quilting.
235|This section explains how to select craft stitch types, as well as change stitch settings to
235|obtain the best results.
235|
235|

235|                                                           toolbar) for candlewick borders.

235|                                                           backstitch borders.
235|      Use Blackwork Border (Craft Stitch toolbar) to
235|      outline blackwork designs.                           Use Stemstitch (Craft Stitch toolbar) for

255|Processing Files of Different Formats
255|
255|
255|
255|By default BERNINA artista saves designs to its native
255|file format, ART. This format contains all information
255|necessary both for stitching a design and for later
255|modification. When opening designs created or saved in
255|other formats, BERNINA artista converts the design
255|information so you can modify it using the full range of
255|BERNINA artista features. Depending on the file type,
255|you may need to provide additional information to
255|assist the conversion process.
255|This section describes how to select conversion options
255|for opening and saving different stitch and outline
255|design formats.

261|Outputting and Storing Designs
261|
261|
261|
261|You can output embroidery designs in a variety of ways —
261|by sending directly to machine for stitching or saving to
261|your machine, a design card or PC.
261|When you send designs directly to the machine for
261|stitching, they will be lost when the machine is turned off.
261|To keep designs, write them to the machine’s embroidery
261|module memory or a design card; or save them to your
261|PC’s hard disk, CD or a floppy disk. Saved designs can
261|then be retrieved and edited in BERNINA artista. You can
261|also delete or rename saved designs.
261|This section describes how to check and print design
261|information, and how to generate different outputs from
261|your designs as well as how to read and write embroidery
261|design files to design cards.

269|Magic Box
269|
269|
269|
269|Magic Box allows you to convert between designs saved
269|in a variety of ‘non-native’ formats. You can read a
269|design from any supported design card into BERNINA
269|artista, edit it then write it to a Magic Card. If you obtain
269|a design from a Magic Card or other design card, you can
269|only write it back to a Magic Card. You cannot save it to
269|your computer or write it to a design card other than
269|Magic Card.
269|The Magic Box software is installed automatically when
269|you install BERNINA artista and only works with
269|BERNINA artista. This section deals with how to use the Magic Box design card
269|conversion software. The instructions included here only apply to the operation of the
269|Magic Box with BERNINA artista. Refer to the Magic Box User Manual for installation,
269|setup and operating instructions.
269|Note too that the instructions cover the use of the serial port Magic Box. For the USB
269|Magic Box see the Bernina/OESD Online Support Center at:
269|http://berninasupport.custhelp.com/cgi-bin/berninasupport.cfg/php/enduser/home.php
269|If you are using a USB Magic Box, you will need to update your BERNINA artista software
269|so that it is using the correct version software. Refer to the latest BERNINA artista
269|Support Notes for more details.
269|
269|

285|Portfolio Basics
285|
285|
285|
285|BERNINA artista Portfolio provides an efficient way
285|for viewing and managing embroidery designs. This
285|design management tool can access design files
285|stored on your computer hard disk, CD-ROM, or
285|floppy disk. Portfolio even lets you archive and view
285|design files in folders which have been archived by
285|means of the popular WinZip utility. It recognizes
285|all design file formats used by BERNINA artista. See
285|Converting design files in folders for details.
285|This section describes the complete workings of
285|BERNINA artista Portfolio from start up to viewing,
285|sorting, and converting designs. It also explains
285|how to use BERNINA artista Portfolio to publish
285|design catalogs.
285|
285|
285|
285|Opening Portfolio and setting
285|defaults                                         Note If you start Portfolio from the desktop or
285|                                                 from the Windows Start button, BERNINA artista
285|BERNINA artista Portfolio does not require a     will also open. If your computer is slow or you
285|separate installation. It works as an integral   have many applications running, Portfolio may
285|part of BERNINA artista and is easy to set up    not open.
285|and get started.
285|
285|                                                 Tip Close Portfolio in View by Details mode so
285|Opening Portfolio                                that it opens more quickly next time.
285|Portfolio may be opened from the desktop or
285|from the Windows Start button.

297|Portfolio Advanced
297|
297|
297|
297|Designs in BERNINA artista Portfolio folders can be
297|sorted in three main ways. This is useful when you
297|want to select designs for stitching out, printing,
297|archiving, and so on. Once a design is selected in
297|an Portfolio folder, you can send it direct to an
297|embroidery machine. You can also convert your
297|ART and other design files to and from other file
297|formats directly from Portfolio.
297|Catalogs of designs in a folder contain thumbnails
297|and/or summary information. These can be sent to
297|a printer and published in a variety of formats.
297|Portfolio lets you archive and view design files in
297|folders which have been archived by means of the
297|popular WinZip utility. This can be useful for sending or receiving multiple files via email.
297|This section describes the more advanced workings of Portfolio from sorting files to
297|stitching, and converting designs. It also describes how to print and publish catalogs of
297|designs, as well as how to archive dormant or unused designs.
297|

309|                                                                       Chapter 34
309|
309|Introduction to Cross Stitch
309|
309|
309|
309|Cross stitching is a popular technique for filling large areas with
309|low stitch counts. It can also be used for outlines and borders.
309|It is suitable for homeware, tablecloths, children’s clothes and
309|folk designs. Cross stitch is sometimes combined with appliqué.
309|Unlike machine embroidery where designs are enhanced with
309|different stitch types, angles, and effects, in cross stitch you
309|can only add dimension to the design with shades of colors. For
309|this reason, most cross stitch designs use many more colors
309|than machine embroidery.
309|This section provides an overview of the various cross stitch
309|types.
309|
309|
309|
309|
309|Types of cross stitch
309|Cross stitches are created on a matrix of              Full Cross         Upright Cross
309|squares or ‘pixels’. Any part of the square can
309|be stitched, from the edges to the diagonals.
309|                                                       Three-Quarter
309|The full range of cross stitches is listed below.                         Double Cross
309|                                                       Cross
309|
309|                                                                          Elongated
309|                                                       Half Cross
309|                                                                          Vertical Cross
309|
309|
309|
309|
309|BERNINA® artista Online Manual                                                        307
309|
310|                                                                  Chapter 34: Introduction to Cross Stitch
310|
310|
310|                                   Elongated
310|         Quarter Cross             Horizontal                                           three-quarter cross
310|                                   Cross                                                stitch pattern
310|
310|
310|         Mini Cross                Single Line
310|
310|
310|         French knot
310|
310|
310|
310|Cross stitch fills                                    Note The long arm of the three-quarter stitch
310|                                                      can go either / or \ directions.
310|When using cross stitch as a fill you can select
310|                                                      Frequently a quarter stitch and a three-quarter
310|from any of the cross stitch fill types.
310|                                                      stitch of different colors share a single square.
310|                                                      Mix and match their positions to give different
310|Full cross stitch                                     effects.
310|Full cross stitches are made up of two
310|equal-length stitches that cross at the center to
310|form an X. The overall effect of the fill depends
310|on which stitch in the X lies underneath or on
310|top. You can also mix and match for special
310|effects.
310|
310|
310|                                                            mixtures of quarter and a three-quarter stitches
310|                                 full cross stitch
310|                                 pattern
310|
310|                                                      Half cross stitch
310|                                                      A half stitch is simply a diagonal stitch that looks
310|                                                      like / or like \. Half stitches are usually used for
310|                                                      shadows and background shading. The stitch
310|                                                      can start from any corner. Sometimes two half
310|                                                      stitches of different colors are used to make one
310|Three-quarter cross stitch                            full cross stitch.
310|A three-quarter stitch is most often created by
310|stitching a quarter stitch followed by a half                                               half cross stitch
310|stitch. A different effect is achieved by stitching                                         pattern
310|the half stitch first and anchoring it with the
310|quarter stitch.
310|
310|
310|
310|
310|BERNINA® artista Online Manual                                                                                  308
310|
311|                                                                Chapter 34: Introduction to Cross Stitch
311|
311|
311|Half cross can go in either direction depending
311|on the effect you want to achieve. For example,
311|half cross used to represent feathers would                                        upright cross stitch
311|                                                                                   pattern
311|slant in the direction of the feathers themselves.
311|
311|Quarter cross stitch
311|Quarter stitches are used to stitch more
311|intricate patterns.
311|
311|
311|                              quarter cross stitch
311|                              pattern                Double cross stitch
311|                                                     Double cross stitch is two full cross stitches
311|                                                     stitched at 90º on top of each other. A double
311|                                                     cross stitch resembles a star. It is generally used
311|                                                     in a scattered fashion or worked into a row to
311|                                                     form a decorative border.
311|
311|
311|                                                                                   double cross stitch
311|Mini cross stitch                                                                  pattern
311|Mini cross stitches are two equal-length stitches
311|that cross at the center to form an X but they
311|only fill quarter of the square. Use mini cross
311|stitch for details such as eyes or for a denser
311|look in parts of your design.
311|
311|                                                     Typically the top thread of the bottom cross is
311|                              mini cross stitch
311|                              pattern                the stitch which lies at 135º to the horizontal;
311|                                                     and the top thread of the overlapping cross is
311|                                                     the horizontal stitch.
311|
311|                                                     Elongated cross stitch
311|                                                     Elongated cross stitch consists of two
311|                                                     equal-length stitches that cross to form an X.

315|                                                                            Chapter 35
315|
315|Cross Stitch Essentials
315|
315|
315|
315|In BERNINA artista Cross Stitch you can
315|add cross stitches either to an entire
315|design or selected areas. Or you can
315|place them individually. There are two
315|stitch types, outline and fill. An outline
315|stitch can be a single run, or a line of
315|cross stitches. A fill can be any of the
315|cross stitch types. You can pre-set stitch
315|type, length and the number of times each stitch is sewn.
315|This section describes the use of the cross stitch design window, techniques for manual
315|cross stitch digitizing, and cross stitch design file handling.
315|
315|
315|
315|Opening Cross Stitch                                   The Cross Stitch design window opens.
315|

315|       Click Cross Stitch (Design toolbar) to launch
315|       the Cross Stitch application.
315|
315|Cross stitch design involves a different digitizing
315|technique to ordinary embroidery design. For
315|this reason, the cross stitch application has its
315|own design window which you open from within
315|BERNINA artista.
315|

329|                                                                             Chapter 36
329|
329|Cross Stitch Editing
329|
329|
329|
329|BERNINA artista Cross Stitch provides techniques for
329|editing cross stitch designs, including moving, rotating, and
329|mirroring stitch blocks. You can erase stitches as well as
329|change colors and stitch types of selected areas. You can
329|clone a selection for re-use as a ‘rubber stamp’ and fill large
329|areas with motifs or special composite stitches. You can also
329|edit stitches to create combinations of partial crosses
329|comprised of multiple colors.
329|This section provides details of cross stitch editing features.
329|
329|
329|

329|provides a number of ways to select cross               Use Select Object (Design toolbar) to select
329|                                                        a single stitch or block of stitches.
329|stitches. It also lets you lock cross stitches
329|and/or outlines so that they are not moved or           Use Polygon Select (Design toolbar) to select
329|edited by accident.                                     irregular areas or shapes.

329|                                                 The Select Object and Polygon Select tools work
329|                                                 in a similar way to BERNINA artista. The
329|                                                 difference is that in BERNINA artista Cross
329|                                                 Stitch you work with stitch blocks or areas
329|                                                 rather than design objects.

379|                                                                      Appendix G
379|
379|Alphabet Samples
379|
379|
379|
379|The embroidery alphabets shown in this appendix are a part of your BERNINA artista
379|program. For the best results when stitching, do not exceed the maximum or minimum
379|sizes recommended for each of the individual alphabets. For actual embroidery
379|alphabets and instructions on how to use them, see Adding lettering to embroidery
379|designs.
379|For best results, always check that the correct type of underlay is selected. Small,
379|narrow letters may not require automatic underlay, depending on their size and the
379|fabric to be stitched on. For example, Anniversary is a very small letter which will stitch
379|at a minimum of 5mm. If auto underlay is used, it will show outside the stitched
379|columns. Therefore underlay should be turned off. See also Switching off auto underlay
379|for small lettering.
379|A SpecialAlphabet template for manually stitched alphabets — Creative Cross and
379|Quilting Text — has been included.

495|Glossary
495|
495|
495|
495|This glossary contains many embroidery and computing terms which you may meet
495|while using your BERNINA artista software.
495|Active window: The active window is one to             Artwork: Bitmap image used as a backdrop for
495|which the next command or action will apply. If        digitizing.
495|a window is ‘active’, its title bar changes color to
495|differentiate it visually from other open              Artwork preparation: The Reduce Colors
495|windows.                                               feature automatically reduces color blocks in
495|                                                       bitmap images to a single color, removing
495|Alphabet: A set of characters of the same              anti-aliasing and noise. You can let the software
495|design or style including letters, numbers and         reduce the color count automatically or specify
495|typographical symbols.                                 a precise number. The latter is useful if you want
495|                                                       to match design colors to an exact number of
495|Anchor point: A fixed point used when                  thread colors.
495|rotating, scaling, skewing or mirroring a design.
495|                                                       ARX: BERNINA artista Cross Stitch format.
495|Anti-aliasing: A software technique similar to
495|dithering which is used to soften hard outlines        Auto Appliqué: Auto Appliqué is an embroidery
495|where color blocks intersect. It produces              object associated with an appliqué which
495|smoother outlines by ‘blurring’ the pixels where       provides automatic stitching to place it, tack it
495|colors join.                                           down, and cover its edges.
495|
495|Appliqué: Decoration or trimming cut from              Auto Digitizer: Digitize complete images
495|one fabric piece and stitched to another to add        automatically with Auto Digitizer. Auto Digitizer
495|dimension. APPLIQUE The use of fabrics sewn            automatically converts artwork to embroidery
495|onto one another for decoration that adds              objects and generates stitches.
495|dimension and texture. Designs with applique
495|are economical because they reduce the                 Auto Jump: The Auto Jump feature preserves
495|amount of embroidery stitches needed to fill the       long stitches in an object by splitting them into
495|design area.                                           a series of jumps. This prevents the machine
495|                                                       from inserting unwanted needle penetrations
495|ARQ: BERNINA Quilter format.                           when the maximum frame movement is
495|                                                       exceeded.
495|ART: BERNINA artista format.
495|                                                       Auto-sequencing: The Auto-sequencing
495|Artistic View: Artistic View: a realistic, ‘three      feature lets you digitize like objects — e.g. the
495|dimensional’ preview of a stitched embroidery          fingers of a hand — without having to think
495|design.                                                about the most efficient stitching sequence and
495|                                                       joins.
495|
495|

496|
496|
496|Backdrop: A ‘backdrop’ is an electronic drawing       articles such as hankies, table napkins, table
496|which you can use to digitize designs on-screen.      clothes, and doilies.
496|Two types can be used — vector or bitmap. You
496|can insert them from various file sources, or you     Blanket stitch : Stitch used for edging
496|can copy and paste them via the Windows               applique. Composed of running stitches in an E-
496|clipboard.                                            or comb-shape.
496|
496|Background: The area inside the active                Block: The basic unit of a quilt top.
496|window.                                               BMP: Windows Bitmap image format. See also
496|Backing: The ‘backing’ is the woven or                Bitmap.
496|non-woven material used beneath an item or            Border: A border is a strip of fabric that is
496|fabric being embroidered to provide support and       joined to the inner quilt to enhance it.
496|stability. It can be hooped with the item or
496|placed between the machine throat plate and           Bounding outline: The dotted rectangle that
496|hooped garment. It is available in various            appears when you select a range of items.
496|weights and types such as cutaway, tearaway
496|and soluble.                                          Candlewicking : A traditional white-on-white
496|                                                      embroidery technique, usually done on white
496|Backstitch: Back stitch is a stitch which can be      linen or cotton fabric with heavy cotton threads.
496|used as a delicate outline. This stitch follows
496|intricate curves well if the stitches are worked in   Checkbox: A small square box that appears in
496|small and in an even manner in order to follow        a dialog and that can be selected or cleared.
496|the flow of the curve.                                When the checkbox is selected, a tick appears in
496|                                                      the box. A checkbox represents an option that
496|Backup: The copying of files onto floppy disk or      you can set.
496|other media so that the data is secure. Usually
496|two copies are made and kept separately.              Click: To press and release the left mouse
496|                                                      button.
496|Baseline: The imaginary line on which the
496|letters of an alphabet sit. (Only descenders          Clipboard: A temporary storage area in
496|extend below it.)                                     memory for what was last cut or copied.
496|                                                      Stitching on the clipboard can be pasted into
496|Baseline Arc Angle: The Baseline Arc Angle            designs any number of times.

504|stitches from extending outside the cover
504|stitches.
504|
504|Underlay stitch: Stitches laid down before
504|other design elements to help stabilize fabrics
504|The stitching action that will attach the backing
504|to the fabric being embroidered. It also supports
504|the top embroidery for a more lofty, dimensional
504|look. Underlay stitches are made up of a series
504|of single run stitches, usually with a very short
504|stitch length, and are digitized manually or
